chunks: From him, from several of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Abd al-Karim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
I said to him, 'A man permits the private part of his slave-girl to his brother.' He said, 'Yes, for him whatever he permitted from her.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a man permits his brother to have intercourse with his slave-girl?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Istibsar clarifies the fiqh of 'Ihala' (granting permission), establishing that a master's right to share his slave-girl with another man is derivative and strictly bounded by the scope of his own ownership. It highlights the Shia juristic principle that the secondary party's rights cannot exceed the primary owner's granted authority, a nuance critical in distinguishing between full concubinage rights and limited permission. The narration underscores the precision required in defining the extent of 'what he has allowed,' preventing any assumption of unrestricted access.
